reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview or recently-stabilized APIs are used; every config key and runtime API has been stable across Astro majors 5–7, so the only exposure is the (reasonable) pin to the current stable major.

evidence: app/astro.config.mjs:6-7 — output:'server' + node adapter is required by the spec (fetch all data over HTTP at request time, serve production build on $PORT)
app/astro.config.mjs:8-10 — session:false, devToolbar:false and checkOrigin:false are deliberate stable opt-outs, not novelty
app/src/pages/index.astro:9 — Astro.url.searchParams is the idiomatic stable way to satisfy the URL-query filter-state requirement
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used, and each stable choice maps directly to a spec requirement (on-demand SSR for live API data, port-driven Node server, query-driven filters).

findings.issue: security.checkOrigin:false disables Astro's default CSRF origin check; harmless for this read-only GET app but it removes a default protection for no stated benefit.
findings.suggestion: Drop the security block and keep the default (true), or add a comment explaining why cross-origin form posts can never occur.

findings.issue: session:false is a no-op — sessions are off unless a driver is configured in current Astro, so the line is config noise.
findings.suggestion: Remove the session line to shrink the config surface.

summary: The app is deliberately conservative: it runs on the current stable Astro 7.4.x but touches none of Astro 7's new or experimental surface (advanced routing, CDN cache providers, route caching). Everything used — output:'server', the Node adapter, Astro.params/url/response/props/self — has been stable across majors 5–7, so breakage risk from framework churn is near zero. The only notable choices are two stable-config opt-outs (checkOrigin:false, session:false) that are unnecessary rather than risky.
